neighbours.label: the conjunction (', but' / ', so') that follows a clause stating that something is absent ('has no official flag, but …', 'there was no local unit, so …'); the same slot as code 'else:' in the card. The - pole is the other side: 'because' / 'since' / 'or' continuing a positive clause
fire: The village has no railway station, but a bus runs twice a day.
There was no doctor on the island, so the sick were taken by boat.
The museum has no permanent collection, but it hosts six shows a year.
There is no direct road to the lake, so visitors hike the last mile.
The club had no ground of its own, so matches were played in the park.
The language has no written form, but its songs are widely known.
The school has no library, so pupils borrow books from the church.
There were no survivors of the wreck, but the cargo was later recovered.
quiet: The village has a railway station, and a bus runs twice a day.
There was a doctor on the island because the mine paid for one.
The museum has a permanent collection, which fills six rooms.
There is a direct road to the lake, and visitors drive right up.
The club had a ground of its own, where matches were played each week.
The language has a written form, and its songs are widely known.
The school has a library because a merchant left it his books.
There were many survivors of the wreck, and the cargo was later recovered.

notes: Probes: 'has no official flag, but' 0.96, 'was no local unit … , so' 0.61, 'did not have a ticket, so' 0.29, 'No letters …, and none' 0.19, positive clause + 'and' 0.15, 'because' 0.03. A short 'else:' snippet scored only 0.13, so I test prose only; the code branch of the card is not covered by this test.
